item.title: Q43 - Polygenic Inheritance of Plant Height
item.description:
Theory Sample data — placeholder
Quantitative Genetics, Heritability & Inbreeding

Refer to the question paper for figures and tables.

Q43. If 45 cm is the basal height and a gardener selfs plants with genotype M0M1 N0N2 O0O3 P0P4, what proportion of plants would be 65 cm tall?
1/256 — To reach 65 cm from a 45 cm base requires an additional 20 cm. The selfing parent contributes alleles summing to 0+1+0+2+0+3+0+4 = 10 cm per gamete pair. For exactly 20 cm additional height, the offspring needs allele combinations summing to 20. Each gene independently assorts with probability 1/4 for each homozygous class and 1/2 for heterozygous. The only way to get exactly 20 cm is the genotype M1M1 N2N2 O3O3 P4P4, each with probability 1/4. So (1/4)^4 = 1/256.
← Previous: Q42 Next: Q44 →

item.title: Q45 - Multiple Alleles in Mallard Duck Plumage
item.description:
Theory Sample data — placeholder
Extensions of Mendelian Inheritance

Refer to the question paper for figures and tables.

Q45. If F1 progeny yield 50% restricted, 25% mallard, and 25% dusky ducks, what are the parental genotypes?
M^R m^d x M m^d — The 50% restricted : 25% mallard : 25% dusky ratio requires one parent to be heterozygous restricted/dusky (M^R m^d) producing M^R and m^d gametes equally, and the other to be heterozygous mallard/dusky (M m^d). The cross gives: 1/4 M^R M (restricted), 1/4 M^R m^d (restricted), 1/4 M m^d (mallard, since M > m^d), 1/4 m^d m^d (dusky). This produces 50% restricted, 25% mallard, 25% dusky.

item.title: Q46 - Epistatic Coat Color in Rodents
item.description:
Theory Sample data — placeholder
Gene Interactions: Epistasis & Complementation Analysis

Refer to the question paper for figures and tables.

A. If a true-breeding brown rodent (SSBB) is crossed with a completely recessive rodent (ssbb), what is the F2 phenotypic ratio?
9 brown : 3 black : 4 pale — F1 from SSBB x ssbb = SsBb (all brown). F2 from SsBb selfing: 9 S_B_ (brown), 3 S_bb (black), 3 ssB_ (pale), 1 ssbb (pale). The ss genotype is epistatic to B/b (no pigment regardless of B allele), so 3 ssB_ + 1 ssbb = 4 pale. Final ratio: 9 brown : 3 black : 4 pale.
Bi. Cross (i): 7 brown : 7 pale offspring from brown female x ssbb male. Maternal genotype?
SsBB — The 1:1 ratio of brown:pale indicates segregation at the S locus only (Ss x ss gives 1/2 Ss : 1/2 ss). All pigmented offspring are brown (no black), meaning the mother must be BB (all pigmented offspring get at least one B). Maternal genotype: SsBB.
Bii. Cross (ii): 8 brown : 9 black offspring from brown female x ssbb male. Maternal genotype?
SSBb — All offspring are pigmented (no pale), meaning the mother is SS (all offspring get S). The 1:1 brown:black ratio indicates Bb x bb segregation. Maternal genotype: SSBb.
Biii. Cross (iii): 5 brown : 6 black : 12 pale offspring from brown female x ssbb male. Maternal genotype?
SsBb — The overall ratio approximates 1 brown : 1 black : 2 pale. Mother is Ss (half pigmented, half pale) and Bb (among pigmented, half brown, half black). Ss x ss gives 1/2 S_ : 1/2 ss. Among the S_ offspring, Bb x bb gives 1/2 brown : 1/2 black. So 1/4 brown : 1/4 black : 1/2 pale. Maternal genotype: SsBb.
← Previous: Q45 Next: Q47 →

item.title: Q47 - X-linked Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome Probability
item.description:
Theory Sample data — placeholder
Sex Determination & Sex-Linked Inheritance

Refer to the question paper for figures and tables.

A. The probability that V-1 is a son affected with the disease is:
0 — Based on the pedigree, the father in generation IV is unaffected and hemizygous normal (X^A Y). Since sons inherit their X chromosome from their mother, and their Y from their father, the probability depends on the mother being a carrier. From the pedigree analysis, there is no path for the mother to be a carrier, making the probability of an affected son 0.
B. The probability that V-2 is a daughter and who is not a carrier for the trait is:
1/8 — The probability of being a daughter is 1/2. The probability of a daughter not being a carrier depends on the mother carrier status. From the pedigree, if the mother has a 3/4 probability of not being a carrier, then P(daughter and not carrier) = 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8 (considering the specific pedigree relationships).
← Previous: Q46 Next: Q48 →
